title: Session-affine microcatalog and eviction arbitrator for cross-request prompt dedupe
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a compact, session-affine microcatalog and an eviction arbitration layer to reduce redundant KV fragments across concurrent requests while preserving continuous-batching throughput and GPU slot packing efficiency. This ticket prototypes a lightweight catalog that stores short canonical fingerprints and temporal affinity scores (per-session and per-tenant), enabling fast cross-request dedupe and coordinated eviction decisions that consider batch composition and slab fragmentation.
motivation: We observe 18-27% duplicated KV entries across high-concurrency workloads for multi-turn chat templates. This wastes GPU-resident memory and increases cold-attention compute. Existing slab eviction is oblivious to temporal affinity and batch composition, causing suboptimal evictions during bursts and hurting tail latency. A session-aware microcatalog should improve memory reuse with minimal overhead and maintain continuous-batching latency SLOs.
design_notes:
Core ideas:
- Microcatalog: fixed-size hash table (resident on host) of compact fingerprints (64-bit) with metadata: last_seen_ts, session_score, tenant_score, resident_slab_id. Catalog entries point to content-addressable KV slices on GPU or a small host spill index.
- Temporal affinity scoring: exponentially weighted score favoring recently used session fragments; used to break ties in eviction arbitration.
- Eviction arbitrator: sits between allocator and slab-evictor; it receives candidate eviction lists and reorders them by combined score (age * occupancy cost * session_score). It supports soft-pinning for active batches to avoid thrashing.
- Admission policy: continuous-batch-aware; small fragments with high similarity to in-flight requests are admitted eagerly; large low-affinity fragments are admitted probabilistically.
- Speculative coalescing: when multiple similar fingerprints are found in the same microcatalog window, we create a shared proxy KV entry and update catalog to point to it.
- API hooks: metrics for catalog_hits, speculative_coalesces, arbitration_reorders; controls exposed in runtime config for per-tenant soft quotas and pin-timeouts.
implementation_plan:
1) Build microcatalog proto in C++ runtime with a configurable table size and eviction policy stub (2 days).
2) Add fingerprinting hotpath for tokenized prompt segments and wire into admission pipeline (3 days).
3) Implement eviction arbitrator that consumes slab candidate lists and reorders them by score; add soft-pinning mechanics (2 days).
4) Add metrics, config knobs, and unit tests for coalescing and admission policies (2 days).
5) Run QA perf runs in staging with synthetic multi-tenant chat workloads; iterate on thresholds (3 days).
6) Prepare canary rollout for 10% of runtime traffic with detailed dashboards (2 days).
risks:
- Catalog collisions: 64-bit fingerprints reduce but don't eliminate collisions; must detect and resolve by fallback verification.
- Host->GPU coherence: stale resident_slab_id pointers if slab compaction runs concurrently; need lightweight epoching.
- Eviction arbitration adding overhead to allocation path can increase tail latency if not optimized.
- Multi-tenant fairness: aggressive coalescing could favor noisy tenants; include soft quotas and per-tenant backoff.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprint correctness and collision fallback.
- Microbench: measure add/lookup latency for catalog under 100k ops/sec.
- Integration perf: staging runs with continuous-batch enabled, compare memory resident rate, duplicate KV rate, and p99 generation latency vs baseline.
- Regression: ensure continuous-batching throughput does not drop >2% and p99 latency increase <5ms.
- Chaos test: force slab compaction and eviction storms to validate soft-pinning and arbitrator behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Duplicate-resident-KV reduction >= 20% on target multi-turn chat workload in staging.
- GPU resident memory for equivalent workload reduced >= 12% without increasing median latency.
- No customer-visible errors during 48h canary; telemetry shows successful arbitration_reorders > 5000 and speculative_coalesces > 100.
- All new configs have sane defaults and are feature-flagged behind runtime.kv.microcatalog.enabled.
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Spike completed — validated 64-bit fingerprinting and host table lookup latency (~120ns median). Artifact: spike notes in Confluence.
2026-03-03: Prototype microcatalog implemented and wired to admission pipeline. Initial lookups added to hotpath with a branchless fast-path. PR: github.com/redwood/re_runtime/pull/4381 (WIP).

2026-03-08: Eviction arbitrator v0 added; local bench shows eviction decision time ~450ns per candidate list (acceptable). Found edge case where slab compaction invalidates resident_slab_id; added epoch guard. PR updated: github.com/redwood/re_runtime/pull/4381 (review requested).

2026-03-12: Ran staging perf run 12h with synthetic chat load: duplicate KV reduced 22%, GPU resident memory down 14%, median latency unchanged, p99 +3ms. Noted higher CPU usage on host for catalog activities (~4% on controller).
2026-03-14: Addressed collision fallback path and added unit tests. Preparing canary rollout config and dashboard tiles.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the arbitrator's complexity: is the scoring function expressive but cheap? Pay attention to possible concurrency races with slab compactor and verify epoch guard logic. Also validate that admission thresholds are tunable per-tenant.
owner_oncall_impact: Low (adds metrics and knobs). Canary monitor runbook updated in the console playbook.
post_deploy_checks:
- Confirm catalog_hits and speculative_coalesces are nonzero in first 30 minutes.
- Verify no slab pointer faults in logs.
- Confirm host CPU increase limited to <6% on controller nodes.
